source.text: Weekly and daily bias bullish (P-BIAS-02/03) with price in discount of the controlling range and a named buy-side DOL; daily narrative written before London Open stating: 'bullish toward [DOL] ONLY AFTER London sweeps the Asian low and prints displacement + MSS higher; until then no long models are authorised' (ADV-M10-R03, INT-M11-EX01).
Discount of the daily (and weekly) range (INT-M10-EX01, ADV-M14-C06).
Asian range complete and marked; its low is the expected manipulation target (ADV-M07-R04: Asian high/low most likely raided at London Open).
Daily conditional bias statement written pre-London (P-BIAS-03, ADV-M10-R03).
Asian range high/low marked (P-TIME-02); optional secondary SSL layer: prior day's low just beneath (BEG-M11-EX01 Step 2).
DOL named: Asian high / internal BSL as intermediate, daily/weekly BSL as terminal (P-DOL-01).
Inside the London Open Kill Zone: price sweeps the Asian low (and any secondary SSL layer) (P-LIQ-02) — the daily PO3 manipulation (P-PO3-01).
Bullish displacement away from the swept low (P-DISP-01).
Bullish MSS on the 5-minute (or 15-minute) chart with a body close above the relevant short-term high (P-MSS-01).
Judas reclaim test: price does not reclaim the swept level within ~2-3 LTF candles (BEG-M08-R06).
Mark the London-created bullish FVG / OB in discount (P-FVG-01, P-OB-01); Fibonacci from the sweep low to the displacement high — FVG/OB should overlap the 62-79% band (P-FIB-01).
CE of the London-created FVG (or OB boundary) inside the OTE band, in discount.
Limit at CE (BEG-M11-S01 Step 10a) OR market on 1-minute bullish MSS / rejection at the zone (Step 10b).
Limit at CE (BEG-M11-S01 Step 10a) OR market on 1-minute bullish MSS / rejection at the zone (Step 10b).
Timing: retracement during the remainder of the London kill zone or early New York (INT-M09-EX01).

Beyond the swept Asian low (P-STOP-01 A) — or, alternatively documented, below the London displacement origin (INT-M09-EX01: 'depending on the exact structural reference chosen'). INT-M12-EX01 places the stop beyond BOTH the displacement origin and the Asian low.
Asian range high / displacement high / first internal BSL (partial, e.g. INT-M12-EX01 partial at internal liquidity).
Daily / weekly buy-side DOL (runner), typically delivered in New York (INT-M09-EX01, INT-M10-EX01).
No bullish MSS after the sweep -> London expanding lower = genuine breakdown; no long (BEG-M11-NT01). Sweep-and-go through the Asian low = PO3 failure (INT-M10-R05).
Daily bias retired if London closes below the daily invalidation (Asian low / displacement origin) — reassess before New York (INT-M11-EX01).
During the Asian session/Kill Zone: avoid expecting large directional trades; mark the range only, do not seek entries.

Chasing breakouts of the Asian range during the Asian session itself is a common low-quality behaviour; the Asian range is marked for reference, not usually for aggressive directional trading. Do not force setups in low-conviction dead zones (midday/lunch, late Asian hours); stand aside instead.
When there is no clear narrative or conflicting signals, stand aside regardless of the clock/session timing.

When the expected PO3 fails or a day prints as a non-textbook alternative profile with no clear narrative, the trader does not insist on the original idea and should stand aside if necessary after reassessing the HTF narrative and Draw on Liquidity.

Bias is unclear when: weekly and daily structure conflict without a clear corrective interpretation; no obvious Draw on Liquidity stands out; price is at equilibrium of the relevant dealing range with no displacement; multiple opposing PD arrays are equally plausible; a major news event is imminent and the narrative is suspended. Response: stand aside. Clarity is a precondition for intermediate engagement; trading without a clear bias is gambling with ICT tools.
